verdict.reason: Cerro is worth a quick check for after work (17:00 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  The wind should be manageable, but not a big advantage.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY, after work from around 17:00 is probably worth a quick look at Cerro, but I’d treat it as a check-first session. The cams are showing only fair conditions and it’s more mixed wind than clean, so Surfline and MEO Beachcam are the first things I’ll check before heading out. Tide looks mid-dropping, which can help make the beachy peaks more rippable, but if the lineup looks even a bit sloppy on the cams, I’d skip and save it.

best.explanation: Cerro looks like a fun-sized window for Worth checking, Medium confidence: 0.6-1.1 m, 115 kJ, 8 s period, consistent 79/100, and wind is not fully clear.  A sheltered beachbreak with gentle lefts and rights, somewhat similar to Cantinho but less consistent; this is best for manageable bodyboard waves when north-northwest swell reaches the bay with clean southerly wind; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.  Expect: it can feel softer or less defined than the main peaks, and rocks may appear closer to the west cliffs.
